title: Cap. IX Resp.: Major false for pagan infants — Augustine Enchiridion 99; Vasquez on infants
pass_a_gloss: I answer that the Major of the proposed syllogism as to the infants of the Pagans, who are neither counted in the covenant, nor regenerated in Christ, is openly false. For if to condemn someone on account of original sin alone is to deal by strict right, it pertains that with such it be dealt by strict right. And hence Augustine from the sentence of the catholic Church openly pronounces that the universal human race by so just a Divine judgment is damned in the apostate root, that even if no one were thence freed, no one could rightly blame the justice of God: and that those who are freed ought so to be freed, that from the many not freed, and left in most just damnation, it would be shown what the universal fellowship had merited: and whither also the due judgment of God would lead even those themselves unless his unowed mercy came to help, Enchiridion chapter 99. Nay even Vasquez the Jesuit, who sharply defends predestination from foresighted merits, is yet compelled to confess: If we speak of reprobation by which someone is rejected from the grace of God, in reprobate little ones there was altogether no cause of their reprobation; If speech be of reprobation by which someone is rejected from beatitude, those little ones for whom Divine providence so disposes that no remedy of human industry can be applied were by the decree of God excluded from the kingdom of heaven, immediately after foresight of original sin contracted by them, On 1, question 23, article 3, disputation 89, chapter 6. The Arminians therefore advance farther in defense of their error than the Jesuits themselves.
pass_b_english: I answer: as to pagan infants — neither in the covenant nor regenerated in Christ — the Major of their syllogism is openly false. If to condemn for original sin alone is to deal by strict right, then with such God does deal by strict right. So Augustine from the catholic Church's sentence (Enchiridion 99): the whole human race is by so just a divine judgment damned in the apostate root that even if none were freed from it, no one could rightly blame God's justice; and those freed ought so to be freed that from the many not freed, left in most just damnation, it would be shown what the whole fellowship had merited — and whither even they would be led by God's due judgment unless his unowed mercy helped. Even Vasquez the Jesuit, who sharply defends predestination from foresighted merits, must confess: if we mean reprobation as rejection from God's grace, reprobate infants had no cause of their reprobation at all; if rejection from beatitude, those infants for whom providence so disposes that no human remedy can be applied were by God's decree shut from the kingdom of heaven right after foresight of original sin they contracted (on ST I, q. 23 a. 3, disp. 89 c. 6). So Arminians push their error farther than the Jesuits themselves.
source_text: Respondeo, Majorem propositi syllogismi quoad infantes Paganorum, qui nec in foedere censentur, nec in Christo regenerantur, aperte falsam esse. Nam si condemnare aliquem ob solum peccatum originale sit stricto jure agere, pertinet est cum talibus agi stricto jure. Atque hinc Augustinus ex catholicae Ecclesiae sententia aperte pronunciat, Universum genus humanum tam justo judicio Divino in apostatica radice esse damnatum, ut etiamsi nullus inde liberaretur, nemo possit recte Dei vituperare justitiam: et qui liberantur sic oportere liberari, ut ex pluribus non liberatis, et in damnatione justissima derelictis, ostenderetur quid meruisset universa consortio: et quo etiam ipsos debitum judicium Dei duceret nisi ejus indebita misericordia subveniret, Enchirid. cap. 99. Quin etiam Vasques Jesuita, qui praedestinationem ex praevisis meritis acriter propugnat, cogitur tamen fateri: Si de reprobatione loquamur qua quis rejicitur a gratia Dei, in parvulis reprobis nullam omnino fuisse suae reprobationis causam; Si de reprobatione, qua quis a beatitudine rejicitur, sermo sit, parvulos eos quibus Divina providentia ita disponit, ut nullum remedium humanae industriae possit adhiberi, fuisse Dei decreto exclusos a regno caelorum, statim post praevisionem originalis peccati ab ipsis contracti, In 1. qu. 23. art. 3. disp. 89. cap. 6. Arminiani igitur longius progrediuntur in defensione erroris sui quam ipsi Jesuitae.
